correctness.rationale: In a basis with A=[[0,I],[0,0]], a commuting B has blocks [[P,Y],[0,P]]; B²=0 is exactly P²=0 and PY+YP=0. A rank-k P has image U, homology complement of dimension s=r−2k, and a complement on which P maps isomorphically onto U. Multiplication then forces the triangular pattern for Y with opposite corner diagonal k-blocks and an unrestricted s-by-s block Q on ker(P)/im(P). For fixed Q there are 2k²+2ks free scalar entries. Projecting the image of B onto the bottom r coordinates contributes k; the upper part over zero is im(P)+Y(ker(P)), which contributes k+rank(Q). The rank-k square-zero P's are counted by choosing the image, a containing kernel, and an isomorphism from the kernel quotient of the ambient space to the image. Counting Q by its image and a surjection gives R_{s,h}; all allowed strata are nonempty, including the dimension-zero blocks. The leading exponent is 4k(r−k)+h(2s−h)=r²−(s−h)² with leading coefficient one, giving maximal rank concentration and both uniform limits at fixed r. Nothing divides by 2, so characteristic two is included.
residual_risks: Archived small-field checks are not independent reproductions here; the block proof covers arbitrary finite fields and is decisive without them.
No claim for nonmaximal A or for r growing with q.
